title: The Weekly: The Binance Hack and What Comes Next
text: NOV 2, 2026 The $6.3bn Binance exploit was the largest crypto hack on record, but its market impact has been far more contained than the headlines suggest. With $2.8bn frozen by Circle and Tether and 95% of affected funds replenished, the response shows how far on-chain infrastructure has matured. This week we look at how crypto beta and alts held up against US tech, why Bitcoin is likely to trade between its 50-week MA and $80k, and how the largest hedge fund de-risking in a decade, falling US 10-year yields and the US midterms could set up renewed risk appetite.  New Institutional Report, written in collaboration with Clear Street. Institutional DeFi needs a common language for risk. Led by Re7 Founder and CIO Evgeny Gokhberg and built on our own methodology, A Framework for Decomposing DeFi Risk in the Age of AI breaks exposure into chain, protocol and asset layers and explores how AI is reshaping risk monitoring. Download the report here . Evgeny Gokhberg joined 1000x Podcast: What It’s Like Running A Billion-Dollar Market-Neutral Fund In Crypto. ▶️ YouTube 🎧 Spotify Bringing corporate treasury on-chain: a conversation with Yuval Rooz on Crypto Minutes, Bloomberg TV. Re7’s Founder & CIO Evgeny Gokhberg hosts a conversation with Yuval Rooz, Co-Founder and CEO of Digital Asset , the company behind Canton Network , on the next phase of finance moving on-chain. For Yuval, RWAs have always been the most compelling use case on-chain, and corporate treasury is where that becomes real: “You’re going to start seeing corporates on Canton very soon using yield products that can be liquidated in real time into tokenized deposits or stablecoins. They’ll start doing treasury management using on-chain finance.” Watch the full episode here . We are hiring! Senior Legal Counsel - Apply here . Crypto Fund Operations Manager - Apply here . We cover: Why the $6.3bn Binance exploit has had a surprisingly limited impact on markets. Crypto sentiment resetting as Bitcoin holds key technical support. Improving cross-asset conditions ahead of the US midterms, potentially setting up renewed risk appetite. Last week’s $6.3bn Binance exploit was the largest crypto hack on record, but we think the headline figure materially overstates the damage. Approximately $2.8bn in stolen assets were rapidly frozen by Circle , Tether and other issuers, while Binance has reportedly replenished 95% of affected funds through its own reserves and insurance fund. The speed of the response demonstrates how the industry’s capabilities have matured, with transparent onchain infrastructure enabling stolen assets to be frozen and traced, materially containing the damage. For perspective, the exploit represented just 3.7% of Binance’s $171bn in customer assets, with the ultimate economic loss considerably smaller. More importantly, Sunday’s $3.6bn in net withdrawals represented just 2.1% of customer assets, suggesting that even the largest hack in crypto history has failed to trigger a meaningful run on the exchange. Binance customer assets and net flows following the $6.3bn exploit. Ultimately, the economic and market impact looks far less consequential than the headlines suggest. text:
Binance hot wallet incident: Re7 Labs update

Our risk systems flagged the incident immediately, and the team has been tracking it since the first reports came in.

Re7 curated vaults have no exposure across all chains and platforms to the event and we’ll continue to monitor all positions closely.

Where things currently stand:

- Vault withdrawals are working as normal
- Some Morpho markets could see less liquidity and more volatility over the coming days whilst the market reacts to the event.
- Potential liquidations due to the spiked rates are being monitored and all are expected to run smoothly should any liquidation occur.

We will continue to monitor the situation and have automated emergency procedures in place to react in real-time to any potential further events.
